title: Sep 19 Results + Sep 20 Preview: I've Seen Hotter Streaks, But 73% Will Do
summary: 11-4 on Sep 19 with 73.3% accuracy. Mets-Phillies rematch headlines Sep 20 slate.

content.value:
## Another Day, Another Winning Record

You know, after covering this game for as long as I have, a 73.3% night doesn't make me jump out of my chair anymore—but it sure beats the alternative. We went 11-4 on Friday's slate, and while three misses might sting the younger guys on the beat, I've seen enough September baseball to know that's a solid night's work.

## The Misses Tell a Story

Let's talk about what went wrong before we celebrate what went right. Tigers couldn't get it done in Chicago despite our 52% lean—close calls like that are coin flips anyway. The Brewers-Orioles game flipped on us at 50%, which is basically the model shrugging its shoulders. And Houston? They were 54% favorites against Atlanta and came up short. I've seen the Braves play spoiler in September enough times to not be shocked.

## The Sweet Spot Performed

Our mid-range confidence picks—those 59-63% selections—went 4-for-4. That's where the model earns its keep. Rangers at 63%, Cubs and Nationals both at 61%, Guardians at 59%. All winners. I've been doing this long enough to know that when your comfortable favorites deliver, you're having a good night.

## Looking Ahead to Sep 20

Here's something that caught my eye for Saturday: we're going back to the Phillies-Mets well. After the Mets squeaked out a win yesterday in what was essentially a toss-up, we're leaning their way again—though still at just 50% confidence. Cristopher Sánchez goes for Philadelphia against Jonah Tong for the Mets.

content.title: ⭐ Sep 20 Top Pick
content.value: New York Mets over Philadelphia Phillies
content.sub: 50% confidence · Sánchez vs Tong · Another tight NL East battle

content.value:
## The Veteran's Take

Look, a 50% pick isn't exactly going out on a limb, and I've seen enough Phillies-Mets games to know these divisional matchups in September can go either way. But that's the honest assessment, and after three decades covering this sport, I'd rather give you the truth than pretend we've got some lock.

The Mets have been scrappy at home, and Tong's gotten better as the season's worn on. Sánchez is solid, no doubt, but in a near-even matchup, I've learned to trust the home team with momentum. We'll see if that wisdom holds up come Saturday night.

Stay sharp out there. Tomorrow's another day of baseball, and in September 2026, every game matters.
